bridge: You have used Python variables and functions (P02/P03) and traced HTTP requests (N06). Here the browser runs JavaScript instead of Python. Save the example as greet.html using a plain-text editor, then open that file in your browser. No server or account is needed.
teaching:
HTML describes document structure. The DOM is the browser's live object model of that document. JavaScript reads events and updates nodes. A form is a data-entry structure; its client-side validation improves interaction but cannot enforce server-side trust rules.

Text and markup are different. Assigning textContent inserts literal text, while interpreting a value as HTML asks the browser to parse markup. Use text insertion for untrusted plain text. Later XSS lessons explain why context-specific handling matters when data enters executable or markup contexts.

A web origin is normally scheme, host and port. Paths do not create separate origins. https://notes.example/a and /b share an origin, while changing scheme, host or effective port can change it. Locally opened file URLs have special browser rules, so use the assigned hosted training environment for cross-origin security labs rather than assuming file behaviour matches HTTPS.

An id identifies a DOM element for selectors; a form field’s name identifies its submitted key. They need not match. The form action chooses the destination, and method chooses how fields are submitted; GET normally places the encoded fields in the URL query. Query values are untrusted input, and URL encoding is not authentication or encryption. A submit-button click or Enter can trigger form submission; preventDefault on a submit listener can deliberately keep the interaction local. A click listener on a standalone button is another event.

Keep an explicit visible label associated with an input. Placeholder text disappears as someone types and is not a replacement for that label. The provided script is after its referenced nodes; otherwise use an appropriate loading strategy before querying them. No match from querySelector returns null, so a misspelled selector cannot be treated as an element. Both value and textContent here handle literal text, including angle brackets. Server-side checks remain required even when the local interaction looks correct.

Read the script from outside in. document is the current page; querySelector("#name") finds the element whose id is name. The dot accesses a property or method, just as in Python objects. const declares a variable that will not be reassigned here. addEventListener registers a function to run later when a click happens. The () => { ... } expression is that function; braces surround its body and semicolons separate statements. The script registers the action when the page loads; it reads the input only when the button is clicked.
explanation: The event listener runs after a click. value is text from the input; textContent displays it literally. Typing Fav should show the angle brackets and letters rather than a bold element. This is a harmless way to observe parsing boundaries without running an attack payload.
exercise: Save greet.html and run it. Enter Fav and then the literal text Fav. Record the output and inspect the result node in browser developer tools. Compare origins https://a.example/x, https://a.example/y and https://b.example/x.
solution: The two a.example URLs share an origin. b.example differs. The result contains literal text and does not gain a nested b element when textContent is used.
challenge: Add a Reset button that clears both input and output. Explain why a required input attribute cannot replace a server-side rule that a user may edit only their own record.
